title: Chat & Sessions
description: Single chat, the multi-session grid, voice mode, sub-agents, and how the agent uses your context.

steps.title: The single-chat tab
steps.body:
Chat tab → top center is the message bar, history scrolls above. Each session is a separate conversation with its own memory window. The agent can:

- Read & write files in your home directory
- Search the web
- Run code, query databases
- Look at your projects, business, calendar

Keyboard shortcuts: ⌘/Ctrl+Enter sends, ↑ recalls last prompt, Esc cancels a streaming reply.

steps.title: Sessions = parallel conversations
steps.body:
Each session has a distinct context. Use sessions when you want the agent to *not* mix two threads — e.g. one for `client-A research`, one for `code refactor`. Switch via the threads sidebar.

A session remembers everything inside it (messages + tool outputs) and forgets everything outside.

**Tip:** name sessions descriptively. The agent uses the name when picking which session to deliver an inbound message to.

steps.title: For power users: the multi-session grid
steps.body:
Everyday chatting happens on the **Chat** page. When you want several conversations side by side, open **Grid** from the sidebar. You'll see 4–9 chat panels at once — each with its own session, model, and federation device.

Use cases:
- Run the same prompt across 3 different models and compare
- One session writing code, another reviewing, another running tests
- Talk to the same agent across multiple federated devices simultaneously

Each grid panel has its own model dropdown, federation device picker, and skill picker.

steps.title: Voice mode
steps.body:
Voice tab. Press **Connect** — wake-word + push-to-talk both supported. The agent speaks back through the configured TTS (default: Onyx voice).

If no Claude terminal is selected when you connect, voice mode auto-spawns one so the conversation has somewhere to land.

Settings → Appearance → Voice section lets you change voices, language, and speech speed.

steps.title: Skills + sub-agents
steps.body:
Skills are pre-packaged prompts/tools the agent can invoke mid-conversation. Open the agent-chat sidebar (right edge of any chat), click the lightning bolt → search.

Good examples:
- `/skill ultrareview` — multi-agent code review of your branch
- `/skill watch` — analyze a video file

Sub-agents are isolated agent runs the main agent can spawn for parallel work. The agent decides when to use them; you'll see them in the agent-chat sidebar as separate threads.

steps.title: How the agent uses your context
steps.body:
Every session prepends:

1. The system prompt (sets the agent's behavior)
2. **Your user-profile context** (Settings → Users → Background context)
3. **Your active business** (if you have one set as active)
4. The conversation so far

This is why the user-profile context field is high-leverage: anything you put there flavors *every* session. Update it whenever your focus changes — switching businesses, starting a new project.
